paragraphs: Chapter 430
124th Episode: Elders in Crisis (4)
Smarion Proch.
Jin didn't know much about him. However, as anyone with even a little interest in the history of martial arts would know, he was aware of the fact that Smarion was a near-mutant existence.
Smarion was born into an ordinary peasant family.
However, he was skilled in harming humans from an early age, as if possessed by a murderous spirit, and the first people he killed were his own parents.
He then destroyed the 'Seigalgas' who ruled the Ghost Army for the past several hundred years and planted the flag of Proch in the Ghost Bird Fortress, a legendary figure.
That was Smarion, the father of Lata and Fey.
'Smarion is known to have died when Lata entered his boyhood.'
Jin couldn't readily understand that the owner of this evil spirit was Smarion.
"...What do you mean?"
"My father was a man possessed by an evil spirit since birth. He killed my parents himself and tried countless times to kill me and Fey, his own children."
However, Smarion's attempts to kill the Proch siblings were, like other assassin families or harsh martial arts families, actions for the sake of 'education.'
Although they didn't want to admit it, Lata and Fey knew that they had become stronger because of him. In a sense, Smarion had always been somewhat crazy with results in mind.
"But some of the elders who were close to me, who became the materials for this seal and died, said that at some point, some sort of line disappeared. He became a madman."
Lata added to the explanation.
According to the experiences of the elders at the time, Smarion began to show signs of madness when Lata reached the age of ten.
Smarion was already famous as a crazy killer, but unlike the previous Ghost Army leader, he was famous for treating his subordinates terribly.
That's why the Ghost Army members showed infinite loyalty to Smarion, and Smarion always trusted them.
However, after the 'change' began, his behavior gradually changed.
"They tortured and killed the members and their families in unimaginable, bizarre ways."
"I've never heard of any bad rumors about the previous Ghost Army leader."
"The dead elders thoroughly prevented records and stories from that time from being known to the outside world. He didn't just act maliciously toward his subordinates. He even hurt himself terribly."
"If the previous Ghost Army leader really showed such abnormal signs, it wouldn't have just ended with a rebellion."

"There were several rebellions, they say. They were only suppressed by my father's overwhelming martial arts each time. You probably don't even know that my father had a match with the head of the Runcandel family."
"My father and the previous Ghost Army leader...?"
Jin didn't know that there had been such an incident between Runcandel and the Ghost Army.
In fact, that record was not even stored as a document in the Ghost Bird Fortress and was left as a top-secret document in the Runcandel family, which only the head could check.

"I couldn't see it myself. It happened even before I was born. However, the fight continued for a whole day, and ultimately, victory belonged to Sir Shilon, but for some reason, he didn't take my father's life."
Shilon would not take the life of the defeated.
Jin couldn't easily imagine such a scene, but back then, Shilon must have been young too, so he thought it could be possible.
"After that, Sir Shilon often visited our remote fortress. He would play games with my father or share various stories."
"…Really?"
"Even though I didn't know about that day-long fight, Fey and I saw Sir Shilon and my father drinking together several times."
Shilon was talking and exchanging drinks with someone.
It was a hard image for Jin to picture.
"At that time, the crazy writer also became quite a kind father. He made us siblings sit on his lap and laughed heartily."
"It must be a good memory for you."
"Thinking about it now, my father seemed to want to look good in front of Sir Shilon."
"Do you remember what kind of conversations they usually had?"
What was there between father, Shilon Runcandel, and Smarion Proch? Amid the terrible energy piercing his body, a strong curiosity arose.
"I was too young, so I barely remember the content. However,"
Lata looked at the red seal and continued.

"There is one scene that I remember vividly. I was sitting next to Fey, eating snacks for the first time in a long time, and Sir Shilon was watching us for a moment before asking my father this question."
"Smarion, is everything alright these days?"
"That…?"
"And my father replied like this."
"How could it be alright, Shilon? As you know, I don't have much time left."

"When my father finally became a complete monster like that, and when the elders who used to cherish me became the materials for the seal, I resented my father like crazy. But somehow, that scene came to my mind. My father, who said he didn't have much time left."
At that point, a sudden chill surged.
The day Jin returned from Lafrarosa and became a knight, he had heard the same words from Shilon.
'Not much time left. What on earth does that mean...?'
At that time, he didn't pay much attention to those words.
Precisely, instead of worrying about why Shilon didn't have much time left, he focused more on the meaning contained in those words.
He concentrated on the conclusion that he had to become the lord before Shilon's time ran out.
Smarion. Is everything alright these days?
That thing.
Suddenly, Jin thought that 'that thing' might be the link between Shilon and Smarion.
'Smarion became a monster because of something my father referred to as 'that thing,' and if my father also has the same issue...?'
It could be that the frequent interactions between Shilon and Smarion were for that reason.
As soon as he thought that far, a frightening and terrible assumption came to mind.
'My father could become a monster too, like Smarion Proch beyond this seal.'
He couldn't shake off that assumption, especially because Smarion said 'as you know.' People usually say that when they know the other person is going through the same thing.
His heart pounded, and his blood raced.
"Sir Lata, have you ever heard what 'that thing' my father mentioned is?"
"Unfortunately, I haven't. I've asked the deceased elders several times, but they didn't know either. Only Sir Shilon probably knows."
The Black Sea.
It had something to do with that dark land.
He had a strong conviction that there was a deep connection between Shilon's obsession with the Black Sea and that reason.
'I can find out why my father is obsessed with the Black Sea and what he's looking for there when Luna returns.'
And the monster beyond this red seal could also provide some clues. Of course, it was the biggest weakness of the Ghost Army before it could become a clue.
Jin exchanged glances with Lata as he organized his thoughts.
"Since we can't ask my father right now, we need to find out what 'that thing' is ourselves."
"Yes, my lord."
"But more urgently, it's the escaped elders. They not only have information on this seal, but they also know that I've become an ally of the Ghost Army."
If possible, Jin didn't want to announce to the world that the Ghost Army had become his force for the time being.
Although it wouldn't be bad if it were known, he wanted to show off the extent of 'Jin Runcandel's power' after growing a bit more.
Especially, the Ghost Army needed to maintain a neutral stance and keep the channel open for interactions with external forces.
"That's true."

"The problem is bigger than expected. There's a high possibility that they've already surrendered, but let's hope they haven't yet. Zipple, Kinzelo, the Royal Family, or even Runcandel. If any of them come to Gwigoksaeseong to break this seal, we're in trouble."
"I'm ashamed, my lord."
"I'll send people right away when I get back. Give me a map showing the estimated escape routes and all the information about the traitors."
"Understood."
"And Sir Lata."
"Please tell me, my lord."
Jin smiled and continued.
"Please take care of me from now on."
"The same goes for me."
Meanwhile, while Jin received the loyalty pledge from Lata and the Ghost Army at Gwigoksaeseong,
The elders of Runcandel were holding another gloomy meeting. They were in a situation where the saying "the fire has fallen on their feet" fit perfectly.
"I never thought the Acting Lord would act like this."
"It's impossible. How much blood have we shed for the Acting Lord?"
"Ha, to prove the existence and value of the Elders' Council... What more do we have to do!"
Creak!
As the elders vented their frustration, the door opened.
"Has the Elder Chairman arrived?"
"Elder Chairman!"
"Elder Chairman, have you heard what happened...?"
The person who entered was the Elder Chairman, Jordan Runcandel. The elders had been eagerly waiting for his arrival.
They believed that Jordan would somehow resolve the situation.
If it weren't for the recent series of incidents centered around Jin.

Jordan would have been very pleased with the sight of these old ghosts waiting for him like baby birds. Because they had been intoxicated by the sweet desire for recognition that they had provided so far, they couldn't make proper judgments.
But not anymore.
'These pathetic bastards...'
He felt anger and disgust at their welcoming faces.
Since when?
Since when did the sharpest swords of Runcandel become like this...? He felt as if the bones in his chest were breaking due to overwhelming questions and regrets.
He wanted to cut these rotten scoundrels right away.
However, Jordan didn't forget that they were his biggest remaining support base. And he also remembered the fact that he had been indulging in desires at some point, though not as much as them.
'I, too, and you guys. We must reform and become a pillar of Runcandel again!'
Otherwise, the era of uncertainty, not only ascending the throne but even surviving in the Garden of Swords, has arrived.
"I cannot help but be disappointed in you and myself."
"Elder Chairman...?"
Jordan changed his gaze and looked at the elders.

"It seems that the time has come to regain our lost wildness and vigilance. If we continue like this, we will be eliminated and disappear. From today on, the Elders' Council will never engage in safe fights, so those who are afraid should leave in advance."
